page0.text:
Time passes. It's now 10:00 AM.
I feel much better since eating Sakura's porridge.
The sluggishness I felt this morning is gone.
It doesn't impede my movement, and I think I could go to school if I wanted.

page1.text:
However...
I wonder if this wasn't a cold after all, but maybe the result of serious malnutrition. Just as I make to get out of bed...
"No, don't! You need to rest until your fever goes down, Senpai!"
Sakura rushes over and pushes me down.

page2.text:
"Whew."
And...
Sakura seems so enthusiastic, she made me breakfast, and I still feel pretty slow, so I decide to stay lying down.

page3.text:
After feeding me okayu, she leaves, saying she has something else to do.
Saber's resting in the living room.
She was kneeling in a corner of my room until just earlier, but it was making me nervous, so I asked her to move to the living room.
She protested, naturally, but I convinced her to take up a different guard post just for today.

page4.text:
"Pardon me. How are you feeling, Senpai?"
"A lot better, thanks to you. I still feel slow, but my fever's coming down."

page5.text:
"I'm glad to hear that. You don't need medicine anymore, then. I'll make you something good to eat, so just take it easy."
Sakura goes into the room next door and brings out a new futon.

page6.text:
"What are you doing, Sakura?"
"Giving you a new futon. You were sweating all night, so I thought you'd need a change of bedding."
She lays out the futon next to mine, patting it flat in a practiced motion.
To my surprise, there isn't any dust at all.

page7.text:
"Here it is. Go ahead and change beds, Senpai. Oh, but you should change clothes first. I'll hang your futon out to dry, so please change into these fresh pajamas."
After the futon, Sakura brings out a stack of clean sleepwear.

page8.text:
...
Such...flawless nursing.
This goes beyond mere experience or thoughtfulness.

page9.text:
"It's a genetic skill. It's gotta be baked into your DNA."
"What did you say, Senpai?"
"It's inappropriate, I know, but I'm glad you stayed home from school today.
It's like I'm seeing a brand new side of you, to be honest."

page10.text:
"But of course! It's already been a year and a half, so I know everything about your house."
Sakura proudly puffs out her chest.
Her confidence and positivity feels infectious.

page11.text:
"All right. Then take care of the bed. I'll be a good patient and follow orders."
"You can count on me! I'll peel some apples for you once I hang up the futon, so look forward to it!"
Sakura goes into the hallway, carrying the futon I've been sleeping in.

page12.text:
"Wow. She took everything with her."
Impressed by her high spirits, I change into the pajamas she brought me.

page13.text:
Now, then...
I dry myself off with a towel, change into clean pajamas, and obediently get back into bed to wait for Sakura.

page14.text:
How long is this all taking, I wonder?
Sakura peels me an apple as promised, I enjoy snacking on it, and...
"Oh, Senpai. I said not to push yourself."
...she scolds me even though I feel better now, so I lie back down.

page15.text:
"So Saber helped you?"
"Yes. She said she was tired of doing nothing, so she saved me the trouble of cleaning the guestroom."
"Huh. I'd like to see Saber wringing out some washcloths.
So she pushed a washcloth up and down the hallway?"

page16.text:
"Yes, we both worked hard. Saber said that she learned a lot."
Sakura smiles, looking slightly troubled.
She might have gotten used to Saber, but she still seems to be getting used to dealing with her.

page17.text:
"...Okay. Anyway, good work. But don't work too hard. You're still recovering, too. It's already a lot of effort just to take care of me, so you don't need to worry about cleaning, too."
"That isn't true. I spent the morning here, and I'm going to feed you dinner, too. It only makes sense that I'd clean while taking care of you. After all, I..."

page18.text:
I'm part of this family, too.
Sakura mumbles under her breath, not wanting to sound rude by wishing it was true.

page19.text:
"That's right. You, Fuji-nee, and me, we're like family."
"Huh? Senpai?"

page20.text:
"Sorry for keeping you at a distance. If you're family, then it's only normal for us to take care of one another.
I know I'd look after you too if you collapsed, no matter how awkward it makes you feel.
So, I'm the one being silly for trying not to impose."
I apologize.

page21.text:
...
The conversation stops.
After a moment's surprise during which Sakura held her breath...

page22.text:
"Yes. I'm glad you know that. I think you're a little overprotective of people sometimes."
She smiles happily and straightens out my sheets for me.

page23.text:
...
It made me realize something, finally.
How beautiful this house is.
The reason we've been tending to the unused rooms without even really thinking about it, how lively and lived-in it feels, just like when my old man was still around.

page24.text:
My underclassman at school. My friend's little sister.
That's what Sakura was to me when we first met, but she's been protecting this home even more than I have.
For the last year and a half, the days were truly peaceful.
I took it for granted so much that I never noticed.
Sakura brought me and Fuji-nee something that we never could have obtained on our own.

page25.text:
...
Absently, I look up at Sakura.
Maybe it's because I still have a slight fever, or because Sakura looks so happy taking care of me.
When I see her smile, it warms me up inside and makes me sleepy.

page26.text:
"Mm..."
Huh, I'm pretty sleepy.
It feels...nice. I feel bad for sleeping until lunchtime, but for now, I think I'll close my eyes and...
"But Senpai? That's what I love about you."

page27.text:
"Eh?"
I think she just said something that would send my heart aflutter.

page28.text:
"S-Sakura?"
"S-Senpai!?
You were awake!?"
Sakura backs away from me in a panic.
If she reacts like that, it only makes me blush. In fact, I'm worried I'm going to spike another fever.

page29.text:
"Ah, uh, um, Sakura—"
"I-I didn't say anything! Nothing at all! I was just watching your face because of...your fever! Yeah, I was about to take your temperature!"
She hastily takes out the thermometer and looms over me.

page30.text:
"Senpai, this is a thermometer! I-I'm going to take your temperature, so open your mouth!"
The thermometer inches threateningly towards me, its holder losing her composure.

page31.text:
"Eherm?"
I feel something squishy.
...It only brushed me, but it was Sakura's chest.

page32.text:
...
My brain reaches its boiling point.
Sanity begins to crack under the strain of forbidden memories springing back to mind, and the sensation of an all-too-real female.

page33.text:
"Whoa!
W-wait, Sakura, time out!"
"Kyah!?"
I make a last-ditch effort to roll out of bed.
My body slides out of the futon. My first priority is to get away from those boo—I mean, away from Sakura!

page34.text:
"S-Senpai...? Um, I want to check your fever."
"I'm f-fine! I can do it myself, so stop right there!"
"...? If you say so.
Here's the thermometer—"

page35.text:
"Nooo!
Not right now! Just give me a minute to calm down! If you get any closer, it'll remind me of last night's dream and I'll die!"
I make a stop sign gesture, my face beet red.

page36.text:
But.
"Last night's dream?"
I must be acting really weird, because Sakura suddenly gives me a dubious look.

page37.text:
"Ah...oof. Um, I had a bad nightmare.
I'm trying not to think about it, so I need you to stay over there. J-just saying, but you didn't do anything wrong. I'm the one who lacks training."

page38.text:
"Uh-huh. Training, you say...?"
Sakura watches me vacantly.
...Anyone would, after hearing something like that.

page39.text:
"Um, Senpai, what kind of dream was it?"
"Urgh."
Like hell I can answer that!

page40.text:
"It was n-no big deal. Just a bad dream."
"Senpai..."
Oof. Sakura's eyes become concerned.
...I can't lie to her. But I also can't tell her the truth.
So, I...
